jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.description:
About Lemon.io

Lemon.io is a profitable, growing talent marketplace that connects vetted senior engineers with companies that need them. We’ve been in business for 10 years, have 60 people across Ukraine, Europe, Canada, and the US, and process over $16M in annual GMV. We compress the traditional 2–5 week hiring timeline down to 24–48 hours through a curated, pre-vetted supply of developers.

Hiring is still broken. Recruiters spend weeks building candidate pipelines on traditional platforms, burning energy on unqualified leads. We’re building the product that changes that. Giving recruiters qualified, vetted candidates within 24 hours without the grind. This is a pivotal moment: we’re transitioning from a services-driven marketplace to a technology-driven platform. We need an engineering leader who can drive that transformation.

 

The Role

You will own engineering at Lemon.io. You’ll lead a growing team of engineers, make critical architecture and prioritization decisions, and be directly accountable for the speed and quality of what we ship. This is not a management-layer role. You’ll be hands-on, deeply involved in product decisions, and working side by side with the founder.

 

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the technical roadmap and make sure every engineering effort maps directly to business impact. No features for features’ sake.

  • Lead and grow an engineering team that ships fast, iterates constantly, and treats complexity as a cost.

  • Tackle the hard, multi-layered problem: automated vetting, intelligent matching at scale, demand-side bottlenecks. And figure out where the real leverage is.

  • Make hard prioritization calls. Decide what we build, what we skip, and what we kill.

  • Work directly with the founder and product team to define what success looks like before writing a single line of code.

  • Build the engineering culture: high ownership, high speed, low bureaucracy.

Who You Are:

  • Product-minded, business-first

  • Obsessed with simplicity

  • First principles thinker

  • Fast. Bias toward action

Experience:

  • You’ve led engineering teams (5–30+ people) at a startup or high-growth company.

  • You have hands-on experience with modern stacks and are comfortable with AI/ML tooling.

  • You’ve worked in a distributed, async-first team.

Why Lemon.io:

  • Profitable and growing. No fundraising pressure, real business fundamentals.

  • A pivotal moment: you’re not maintaining an engine, you’re building one. The product roadmap is wide open.

  • Direct access to the founder. No layers. Your decisions ship.

  • A massive, unsolved problem: hiring is still broken. We’re building the product that makes it radically faster for companies to find qualified engineers.

  • A team of 60 people who move fast, care deeply, and have survived the hard years together.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
Consequential Work. Dedicated People.


About Onebrief

Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination.

Military planning is complex by nature, requiring teams to coordinate information, people, and decisions across systems and locations. Onebrief brings planning, collaboration, simulation, and AI into one connected environment, helping teams test strategies, adapt to changing conditions, and make decisions with greater clarity when the stakes are real.

We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world.

Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth.

Why This Role Exists

As a Solutions Engineer at Onebrief, you work where mission, engineering, and compliance meet.

You'll own technical solution design and deployment readiness, translating customer requirements into secure, scalable deployment architectures. You'll partner with Platform Engineering, SRE, and our Cybersecurity team to validate infrastructure, configure environments, resolve technical blockers, and successfully transition solutions into production.

Youâll work with our go-to-market and customer facing teams to meet with planners, operations officers, and network owners to understand how they work today. Youâll help show them what that work looks like in Onebrief, and then you'll make it real.

You connect a staff's planning problem to a live, accredited Onebrief deployment.

What You'll Do

Core responsibilities:

  • Run technical discovery. With Sales and Engineering, map a staff's current workflow and pain points, specifically focusing on their technical constraints: networks, hosting, identity, and integration requirements, especially in multi-network environments.

  • Lead deployment engineering. Coordinate the technical delivery of new deployments, including infrastructure validation, network configuration checks, and system readiness verification. Write code to configure new deployments and support new environments.

  • Support accreditation. Help create and review security documentation, including STIG checklists and ATO artifacts, alongside our cybersecurity team so deployments are accredited on the customer's timeline.

  • Align stakeholders. Get technical stakeholders on both sides to agree on requirements, constraints, and tradeoffs, so customers see value sooner. Ensure those technical requirements are properly translated into contract deliverables.

  • Scope integrations. Design how Onebrief Connect fits into a command's ecosystem: APIs, data pipelines, Foundry and Maven Smart System, CUOPS tools, and dashboards.

  • Deliver tailored demos. Lead technical demonstrations and solution validation, partnering with Sales and customer-facing teams to demonstrate Onebrief's technical capabilities, deployment architecture, security posture, and integration options.

  • Run pilot deployments. Configure Onebrief in new and untested environments to enable limited uses in support of new sales.

  • Turn field experience into patterns. Convert what you learn in deployments into structured workflows and reusable implementation patterns, and feed clear requirements to Product and Engineering.

  • Travel 30â50% of the time to customer sites and exercises.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility.

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

  • 4+ years in solutions engineering, infrastructure or deployment engineering, or forward-deployed engineering, working closely with go-to-market and operational teams

  • Experience in DoW environments and their security and compliance requirements (RMF, STIGs, ICD 503)

  • Strong expertise with containers (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes)

  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and on-premises virtualization (RHEL)

  • Solid understanding of networking concepts and protocols, and of security best practices for highly sensitive environments

  • Strong presence with customers, from action officers to senior leaders, and clear, concise writing

  • Calm under pressure, and focused on forward motion

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proficiency in a scripting language (Python, Go, or Bash)

  • Infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible)

  • Monitoring and logging tools (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Datadog) and service mesh (Istio, Linkerd)

  • Experience as a military planner or staff officer, or with mission command systems, Foundry, or Maven Smart System

  • Presales experience, including building and delivering demos


Notice to Third Party Recruitment Agencies
Please note that Onebrief does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of an executed Recruitment Services Agreement, there will be no obligation to any referral compensation or recruiter fee. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without an agreement Onebrief explicitly reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers, shall be deemed the property of Onebrief.

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

 

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

 

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

 

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.

Requirements

 

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering

  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words

Nice to have

jobs.title: Head of Technology
jobs.description:

Original job posting link

About garden3d

We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.

Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.

Weâre the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer - Development

At Sanctuary Computer weâre building a different type of technology shop â one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX - Design

When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and weâve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

Weâre building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.

Index - Community

Index is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.

We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.

garden3d TK â Media

At garden3d, weâre in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.

We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.

Plus, our partner organizations

Lightphone
Mill
IngredientAI

â°ï¸ The Head of Technology Role

The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.

They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.

Responsibilities & Mandates

ï¸ Systems that hold up

We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.

All in on agentic development

The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering

We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.

Code quality at Sanctuary Computer

Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.

Hiring and empowering the very best

They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

Estimation, scoping and delivery

They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.

The technical voice in new business

Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.

Hardware sense

We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.

The garden3d technology story

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off

Â Special Projects

In addition to day to day responsibilities, hereâs an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years â

  • Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts
  • Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from
  • Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do
  • Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio
  • Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products
  • Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed

Qualifications

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:

Must have:

  • 12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company
  • Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products
  • A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native
  • A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure
  • All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase
  • Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir & Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it
  • Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients
  • A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them
  • Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)

Nice-to-have:

  • A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products
  • Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)
  • Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role
  • Open source projects they've started or maintained
  • Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams
  • Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company
  • A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring
  • Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality

Who you are

The person weâre looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. Theyâre flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work âsmartâ by carefully managing their workflow and team.

How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, weâll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where weâre going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

Compensation

This is a permanent leadership role. If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.

We start with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between $110 - $175 p/hr pending seniority & experience. In the first few weeks of the trial, this individual will propose their own goals to define success in their trial, and present them to our leadership team for approval.

At garden3d, we believe that those who shoulder the most responsibility and create the greatest impact should be paid accordingly. This role greatly favors autonomous, competent & ambitious operators.

â How we work:

  • Transparency & Ownership:Â We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. Weâre proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community.

  • Async & Decentralized: We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time.

  • Ideas & Products:Â In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify & bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio?

jobs.description:
The Role

We've grown to roughly 265 people working onsite from our Menlo Park headquarters, supported by a large network of remote U.S.-licensed clinicians â and part of the Series C is earmarked for acquisitions. The systems and the spaces holding all of that together were built for a much smaller company. We're hiring a Director of IT & Workplace to own them properly.

You'll own two halves of the same problem: the employee technology platform â identity, endpoints, networking, the SaaS portfolio, and our IT security posture â and the physical environment the company runs on, from space planning and physical security to the AV that customer demos and all-hands depend on. You'll inherit a small, capable team and be accountable for leveling it up. You'll be the named owner for IT controls in our HIPAA and SOC 2 programs, you'll own the IT and workplace budget, and when we acquire a company, you'll be the one integrating it.

Our Environment

  • Identity and access: Okta for SSO, MFA, and lifecycle provisioning.

  • Productivity: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, both in active use across the company.

  • Endpoints: a Mac-primary fleet with Windows machines alongside it, managed through MDM. VDIs included.

  • Internal systems: IRU, plus a growing portfolio of internal and third-party SaaS applications.

  • Workplace: a Palo Alto headquarters with conference room AV and access control, plus a distributed clinician and staff population.

What You'll Do

Strategy, budget, and team

  • Own a multi-year IT and workplace roadmap tied to the hiring plan, and bring it to leadership with clear tradeoffs and funding asks.

  • Own the IT and workplace operating and capital budget: forecast it, defend it in planning cycles, and continuously rationalize license, vendor, and facilities spend.

  • Lead, coach, and grow the existing team â set clear expectations, run honest performance conversations, hire as scope deepens, and build career paths that keep strong people.

Technology and infrastructure

  • Own the identity platform: SSO, MFA, automated joiner-mover-leaver provisioning in Okta, and access governance across every connected application.

  • Own the endpoint fleet and the SaaS portfolio â Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, IRU, and a long tail of business applications â with enforced MDM baselines for encryption, patching, and configuration.

  • Own network and connectivity for the headquarters and the remote workforce, with redundancy appropriate to a company our customers depend on.

  • Replace manual provisioning, access reviews, and device setup with scripted, auditable workflows.

  • Lead major programs end to end: platform migrations, upgrades, office buildouts, and the IT and workplace integration of acquired companies.

Security, compliance, and risk

  • Serve as the accountable owner for IT controls in our HIPAA, SOC 2, and customer security review programs, including evidence collection and audit response.

  • Enforce least privilege across the environment and run recurring access certifications with documented outcomes.

  • Partner with Security on incident response and vulnerability remediation, and with Legal on data handling, retention, and discovery requests.

  • Own business continuity and disaster recovery for corporate systems â write the plans, test them, and fix what the tests expose.

  • Treat protected health information and confidential data with the care our customers and their patients expect. This is non-negotiable in everything we do.

Workplace and facilities

  • Own day-to-day operations of the headquarters, and lead space planning and buildouts against a hiring plan that keeps moving.

  • Manage physical security â access control and badging, visitor management, cameras, and emergency preparedness â aligned with our compliance obligations.

  • Own conference room and event AV, including all-hands and customer visits, to a standard where the technology is never the story.

  • Support remote clinicians and staff with reliable equipment logistics, home office standards, and consistent service regardless of location.

  • Manage facilities, AV, security, and food vendors, plus landlord and lease matters, in partnership with Finance and Legal.

What You'll Bring

  • 8+ years in IT, spanning hands-on administration or engineering and progressively senior ownership. You've done the work you'll now be leading.

  • 3+ years managing IT or workplace teams, including hiring, performance management, and developing people into bigger roles.

  • Proven ownership of an IT function through rapid growth. You've scaled systems and process ahead of headcount, not behind it.

  • Deep technical expertise across identity (Okta or comparable), Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, MDM at fleet scale, and corporate networking.

  • Experience as a named control owner in a regulated environment â HIPAA, SOC 2, or HITRUST â including sitting across the table from auditors.

  • Budget ownership and vendor negotiation experience, with the financial fluency to frame a risk or a funding ask so a CFO can act on it.

  • Workplace or facilities exposure â buildouts, moves, physical security, or lease management â or a genuine appetite to own it and learn quickly.

  • Willingness to stay close to the work. This is a leadership role at a company where the director still unblocks a broken demo when it matters.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience. We weigh demonstrated ability over credentials.

Nice to Have

  • Healthcare, life sciences, or another environment handling sensitive personal data at scale.

  • IT integration of an acquisition, or standing up a function's first access governance or asset management program.

  • Automation depth (Python, Bash, PowerShell) and experience managing devices and infrastructure as code.

  • Certifications such as Okta Certified Administrator, Microsoft 365 Enterprise Administrator, Jamf, CISM, CISSP, or ITIL.

Why Join Hippocratic AI

Reinvent healthcare with AI that puts safety first. Weâre building the worldâs first healthcareâonly, safetyâfocused LLM â a breakthrough platform designed to transform patient outcomes at a global scale. This is category creation.

Work with the people shaping the future. Hippocratic AI was coâfounded by CEO Munjal Shah and a team of physicians, hospital leaders, AI pioneers, and researchers from institutions like El Camino Health, Johns Hopkins, Washington University in St. Louis, Stanford, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and NVIDIA.

Working cross-functionally with Data Engineering, Product, Clinical Operations, and EMR partners, your solutions will transform how clinicians access dataâmoving from external tools and workarounds to seamless, in-workflow decision support via CDS Hooks and real-time APIs.

You will own the technical foundation for Clinical Decision Support (CDS) Hooks, REST APIs, and the architectural patterns that ensure clinical data is accessible, trustworthy, and performant at the moment of care. This role sits at the intersection of healthcare interoperability standards, modern API design, and operational excellence. You will establish reliability metrics and SLAs that ensure CDS Hooks and APIs serve clinician workflows with consistent quality and performance. You will be part of a small, high-performing healthcare engineering team where engineers support each other's growth through mentorship and tight collaboration.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Define and measure clinical impact metrics â adoption of CDS Hooks, clinician interaction rates, workflow integration success, and patient outcome influence

The Opportunity

This is a hands-on role for someone who has spent real time designing for e-commerce brands â emails, landing pages, website sections, and social/ad creative â and can explain exactly why each design choice was made.

You'll design across a portfolio of e-commerce clients, working closely with our email, CRO, Shopify development, and paid media teams. jobs.title: Technical Customer Support
jobs.description:
QuickMail is a cold email and LinkedIn outreach platform for markets you can't afford to burn. Our customers can't easily replace leads that land in spam, which is why deliverability matters more to us than anything else. We have been running since 2014, and we pioneered deliverability technology such as Inbox rotationâ¢ and deliverability AIâ¢.

The Role

We are hiring a technical customer support person with an owner's mentality.

You will own support for QuickMail and Mailflow, our deliverability add-on. There is no first or second line. You are the first and last person our customers talk to.

Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are.

The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking.

This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer.

We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it.

If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you.

What Work Looks Like

You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable.

Every day

  • Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it.
  • Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution.
  • Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform.

Delighting customers

  • Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast, and setting them up for success.
  • Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked.
  • Share customer feedback with the team, ask happy customers for reviews and case studies, and watch NPS for testimonial candidates.

Making support smarter with AI

  • Improve the AI support agent. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off.
  • Write and maintain automated tests, built with AI, that try to break staging before customers do.
  • Use the MCP connections we have in place (Helpscout, GitHub, Postmark, and others) to get an accurate picture of support and find the next thing worth improving.

Keeping the product solid

  • Gatekeep releases. New fixes and features land on staging every week. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected.
  • Report bugs as GitHub issues with everything the developer needs: steps to reproduce, screenshots or a Loom, and any GraphQL or console errors.
  • Captain red alerts. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice.

Running the week

  • Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated.
  • Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps.

Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude.

Who You Are

  • You build rapport fast. You are warm, positive, and relatable in writing and on calls.
  • You are a good communicator. Externally, you can show warmth, empathy and care. Internally, you are able to communicate clearly and concisely about important things.
  • You can operate with minimal instructions. You understand a short brief without every detail spelled out. You can prioritize well (especially when you have a lot on your plate), and get things done without hand-holding.
  • You are comfortable on video. You are natural on live calls with Zoom and Meet, and on recorded video through tools like Loom.
  • Your teammates can always count on you. You say what you'll do and you do what you said.
  • You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity.
  • You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results.
  • You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack.
  • Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive.
  • Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are.

A Plus If You Have

  • Experience with customer facing work, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role.
  • Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup. We can teach this, but a head start helps.
  • Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client.
  • Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report.
  • An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment.

How We Work Together

You'll work directly with the founder and with our lead developer.

Working with the founder can be intense. Here is what that looks like in practice:

  • Replies are short and can come across as harsh. If something written lands badly or isn't clear, ask.
  • Direction can change. The founder may say one thing, then something different a few days later as they learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt.
  • Information should be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if asked.
  • The founder can stay frustrated about a problem until it's solved. That's something they are aware of and working on. You'll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on.
  • The team often thinks fast and interrupts each other when discussing ideas. If that would bother you, this role probably isn't for you.

This role suits someone with high emotional intelligence, who doesn't take things personally, asks when something is unclear, and keeps many things moving at once.

Your schedule can be flexible. If you have a martial arts class every Thursday at 3 pm, go and make up the time later. In return, on the rare occasion the team needs your help on a weekend, we ask you to be flexible too.

Benefits

About Magic Eden and Dicey
Magic Eden reached unicorn status in just 9 months after launch, one of the fastest in history. We built a category-defining NFT marketplace from scratch and proved we know how to move fast. Now we're doing it again. Dicey is our crypto casino and sportsbook platform, targeting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets.

We're a small, fully remote team. We ship fast, we're hands-on with our data, and we're rebuilding how a growth team operates around AI from the ground up.

The role
Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.

This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. It's explicitly AI-native. You'll build workflows, agents, and pipelines to run lifecycle campaigns that would have taken a whole team two years ago. Half the job is identifying the right problem. The other half is running the experiments to find the answer.

What you'll do

Why Now

jobs.description:
More than one million people in the United States today are fighting blood cancer. While a traditional allogeneic stem cell transplant has been the best hope for many, the transplant itself can prove fatal or lead to serious conditions, such as graft vs. host disease. Orca Bio is a commercial-stage biotechnology company redefining the transplant process by developing next-generation cell therapies with the goal of providing significantly better survival rates with dramatically fewer risks. With our purified, high-precision cell therapies we hope to not only replace patients' blood and immune systems with healthy ones, but also restore their lives.


The Senior Specialist, Global QMS will help implement Orca Bioâs global quality management system across all sites. This role will support and lead the internal audit program, supplier management program, and inspection readiness. This role will support the growth and expansion of the global quality program to support manufacturing of our cell therapy products. You will help establish, implement and maintain the audit program across Orca Bio sites to ensure compliance with GxP and regulatory expectations. Your role will support Orca Bios commercial readiness and ongoing clinical programs by managing and facilitating audits, resolving supplier-related quality issues and interacting with quality management teams at the site levels to ensure consistent application of quality systems across the organization.

\n


Responsibilities:
  • Plan, schedule and execute internal audits across all sites and functions in accordance with the internal audit program.
  • Develop audit agenda, conduct interviews, review processes and generate audit reports.
  • Support the global Quality Management Review (QMR) process, ensuring timely data collection, analysis, and reporting to senior leadership.
  • Support the supplier qualification and management program, including risk assessments, supplier audits, and ongoing monitoring to ensure compliance with GxP requirements.
  • Drive global inspection management activities, ensuring cross-functional and site readiness for FDA, EMA, and other health authority inspections.
  • Provide oversight and guidance to site QMR administrators ensuring consistent quality system implementation across all Orca Bio sites.
  • Establish and monitor global QMS key performance indicators (KPIs), oversee trending of quality metrics, and ensure data-driven insights are used to improve quality systems and performance.
  • Partner with IT and business process owners to identify and implement QMS system enhancements, including defining requirements, driving prioritization and ensuring changes are validated and compliant.
  • Review, approve, and provide quality oversight for validation documentation (e.g., equipment qualification, computer system validation, process validation) for global enterprise systems (e.g. MasterControl, ERP systems, Trackwise, etc.) ensuring alignment with regulatory and internal requirements.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional and site leadership teams to drive continuous improvement initiatives, ensuring the QMS evolves in line with business needs and regulatory expectations.


Experience:
  • Bachelorâs degree in a scientific or engineering discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Minimum 5+ years of relevant Quality Assurance or Quality Systems experience in a GxP-regulated environment, with at least 2-3 years in a leadership role.
  • Strong knowledge of global quality regulations and standards (FDA, EMA, ICH, ISO 9001, 21 CFR Parts 210/211/820, EU GMP).
  • Proven experience leading Quality Management Review, internal audit programs, supplier management processes, and validation oversight.
  • Demonstrated success in establishing and trending quality performance metrics and KPIs.
  • Experience supporting and/or administering electronic QMS systems and partnering with IT for system enhancements.
  • Experience working in a multi-site or global quality organization strongly preferred.
  • Excellent organizational, analytical, and communication skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across functional and site boundaries.


\n
$90,000 - $120,000 a year
\n

The anticipated annual salary range for this job is based on prior experience in the role/industry, education, location, internal equity, and other job-related factors as permitted by law. For remote-based positions, this range may vary based on your local market. Full-time employment positions will also be eligible to receive pre-IPO equity and annual bonus, in addition to competitive medical, dental, and vision benefits, PTO, 401(k) plan, life and accidental death and disability coverage, and parental leave benefits. Other perks include subsidized daily lunches and snacks at our on-site locations.

 

Who we are

 

We are driven by a passion for science and compassion for patients. We act with urgency to ensure our treatments are one day accessible to all who need them.

 

We live by our core values of passion, courage, and integrity. Excellence in our work means the chance to unlock a better quality of life for our patients, and with that comes tremendous responsibility.

 

We innovate on a path that hasnât been paved. We embrace an entrepreneurial spirit and take calculated risks to achieve our mission. We arenât afraid to ask âwhy notâ and challenge the status quo.

 

We maintain a start-up culture of camaraderie and leadership by example, regardless of title.

 

Weâre proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and recognize that celebrating our differences creates stronger, lasting solutions that better serve our team, our patients and their healthcare providers.

 

Notice to staffing firms

 

Orca Bio does not accept resumes from staffing agencies with which we do not have a written agreement and specific engagement for a particular opening. Our employment activities, inquiries and offers are managed through our HR/Talent team, and all candidates are presented through this channel only. We do not accept unsolicited resumes, and we rarely outsource recruitment.

jobs.description:
**This position is based in Germany with hybrid or remote working options. Applicants must hold a valid work/residence permit for the respective location.**

Chaos is a leading global software company that provides world-class visualization and design solutions, empowering creative minds to bring ideas to life.

For over twenty years, Chaos has developed innovative technologies serving multiple industries, including architecture and design, media and entertainment, and product e-commerce. Chaosâ solutions help architects, designers, VFX artists/animators, and other creative professionals share ideas, optimize workflows, and create immersive experiences.

Headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, Chaos is a global company with offices in 11 cities worldwide. In 2022, Chaos and Enscape merged, bringing together two industry-leading companies into one. Since then, Chaos has continued to grow with the additions of Cylindo, AXYZ Design, and Evolve Lab, further expanding our expertise and solutions across architecture, design, e-commerce, and AI. For more information, please visit chaos.com.

Role Overview

The Team Lead, Education Sales leads the Education sales team and owns the end-to-end go-to-market strategy for the Education segment, covering both University and Student markets. The role is responsible for driving new institution and student customer acquisition, growing ARR within the existing base, and reducing churn across both segments. The University segment operates through direct, relationship-led sales to institutions, while the Student segment runs as a low-touch, digital-first purchase journey, requiring close partnership with the Ecommerce team to optimise the online funnel, conversion rates, and pricing experience. Reporting to the Sr. Director GTM Strategy & Transformation, this role requires a commercially driven sales leader with a hands-on approach, a track record of owning segment revenue end-to-end, and the ability to coach and develop a team while remaining personally active in deals. The role operates with a high degree of autonomy and suits someone who wants to build and scale a team rather than maintain one.

Main Responsibilities

  • Lead and develop the Education sales team, setting clear individual performance expectations, coaching from the front, and stepping into deals directly where needed to support pipeline and attainment targets.

  • Own and scale a proactive, discovery-led outbound motion to win new institution and student customers, continuously refining outreach cadence and qualification criteria.

  • Drive expansion and retention within the existing student and institution customer base, identifying and executing initiatives that grow ARR and reduce churn.

  • Own ARR and pipeline growth within the University segment through relationship-led, direct sales to institutions, tracking key performance metrics and diagnosing and correcting underperformance.

  • Own ARR and seat growth within the Student segment, which runs as a low-touch, digital-first purchase journey rather than a traditional sales motion; partner with the Ecommerce team to continuously optimize the online funnel, conversion rates, and pricing experience.

  • Own accurate pipeline forecasting and attainment reporting for the Education business, providing reliable visibility into performance for sales reviews and senior leadership.

  • Partner with RevOps, Marketing, Product, and Ecommerce to ensure Education-specific campaigns, content, and product feedback are prioritised and executed effectively.



Required Experience

  • At least 5 years of sales experience within a SaaS or technology environment, including demonstrated experience leading a sales team with direct accountability for team performance and revenue outcomes.

  • Proven track record of owning a direct sales territory or segment end-to-end, from pipeline generation through closed, retained revenue.

  • Experience managing and influencing a low-touch, digital or ecommerce-led purchase journey (funnel, conversion, pricing) is a strong advantage.

  • Previous experience in Architecture, Education, EdTech, or a related vertical is an advantage, but not required.

Required Skills

  • Takes full ownership of commercial outcomes: builds pipeline, closes deals, and drives team performance without waiting to be directed.

  • Leads by example in the field: comfortable coaching team members through live deals and personally engaging in high-priority opportunities where it makes a difference.

  • Translates ARR and revenue data into clear, defensible strategy, is able to identify where performance is off track, diagnose the root cause, and act on it.

  • Communicates with credibility at senior level: presents team results, forecasts, and strategic needs clearly to VP-level and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Able to build effective working relationships and collaborate cross-functionally across Ecommerce, RevOps, and Marketing: driving digital funnel and conversion improvements for the Student segment without direct authority.

  • Operates effectively with high autonomy in a fast-moving environment: sets own priorities, creates momentum without close direction, and holds a consistently high personal bar for execution and results.

  • Familiarity with MEDDICC or a similar sales qualification framework is an advantage.

We welcome people who value teamwork, stick to their commitments and are curious to explore new ways for achieving mastery. If you believe that you are a good match for the job, just send us your CV in English.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer Case Execution
jobs.description:
About Pivotal Health

Pivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape.

Today, many providers face persistent underpayment from health insurance companies, despite delivering high-quality care. While processes like IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) were designed to promote fairness, theyâre often administrative-heavy, time-consuming, and difficult to navigate without the right tools.

Pivotal Health combines software, data, and service into a seamlessly integrated, AI-driven platform that simplifies these complex reimbursement workflows. We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement theyâre entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams.

Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. Weâre building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

About the Role

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join Pivotal's Case Execution team. This team owns critical parts of the case execution workflow, including eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These systems sit at the operational core of how Pivotal delivers outcomes for providers.

This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex, workflow-driven backend problems and working through data-heavy decision logic. The most technically demanding areas for this team are eligibility and batching, and the right person is energized by that kind of work rather than looking to avoid it.

What You'll Do

  • Build and improve core case execution systems: Own backend development across eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These are the systems that determine how cases move through Pivotal's platform and reach resolution.

  • Tackle complex, data-driven backend problems: Work through the decision logic and data-heavy workflows that make eligibility and batching hard, understanding not just how individual systems work, but how they interact across the broader platform.

  • Contribute to workflow orchestration: Build and improve the systems that coordinate how cases are staged, routed, and executed end to end, with a clear eye toward correctness and reliability.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with the Integrations team, Case Strategy team, and other engineering and product partners to ensure systems are well-connected and aligned with how the broader platform operates.

  • Contribute to front-end and admin workflows where needed: The role is primarily backend-focused, but you'll contribute to internal-facing UI and ops tooling where the product requires it.

Who You Are

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience with a strong backend focus

  • Strong engineering fundamentals with hands-on experience building data-heavy, workflow-oriented systems

  • Experience working on complex, data-driven decision logic or orchestration problems: you're comfortable with systems where correctness and sequencing both matter

  • Comfortable operating in a collaborative, fast-moving startup environment where ownership and requirements evolve

  • Python experience; able to work effectively in a Python-based backend environment

  • Self-directed and proactive: you identify problems and drive them to resolution without heavy oversight

  • Strong communicator who collaborates well across engineering, product, and adjacent teams

Extra Credit If You Have

  • Experience with healthcare-specific data or HealthTech systems

  • Exposure to data-heavy architectures or problems adjacent to data engineering without being a pure data engineer

  • Familiarity with tools like Snowflake, dbt, or Databricks

  • Some front-end experience to support admin workflow contributions

Why Youâll Love Working Here

Weâre a collaborative, low-ego team on a mission to make healthcare reimbursement fairer for providers. While we primarily hire around our core hubsâLos Angeles and New Yorkâwe remain open to exceptional talent outside those regions. Remote and hybrid flexibility varies by role and team, and is outlined in each job description.

If youâre excited by solving complex problems and making a real-world impact, weâd love to hear from you.

Benefits Include:

  • Competitive compensation, including equity

  • Full health, dental, and vision coverage

  • Retirement savings plan through 401(k)

  • Flexible time off

  • Opportunities for company-wide connection and events

Ready to Make an Impact?
Weâre building something meaningful; and we want you on the team.

Bring your ideas, curiosity, and drive, and letâs transform healthcare reimbursement together.

Employment Information

Work Authorization

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Pivotal Health is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

Reasonable Accommodations

Pivotal Health provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with applicable laws. If you need assistance during the application or interview process, please let us know.

Background Checks

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of applicable background checks, where permitted by law.

At-Will Employment

Employment with Pivotal Health is at-will and may be terminated by either party at any time, with or without cause or notice, in accordance with applicable law.

Du willst in Microsoft Azure Datenplattformen bauen, die Unternehmens- und Maschinendaten unserer Kunden für Auswertungen und KI nutzbar machen – mit klarer Perspektive zum Principal Architect? Dann lies weiter.

Die KRALLMANN AG ist ein inhabergeführtes Familienunternehmen, 2006 gegründet von Prof. Dr. Hermann Krallmann, emeritiertem Professor der TU Berlin, der bis heute aktiv mitwirkt. Wir bieten Strategieberatung, KI-Beratung und -Implementierung, Business Process Management, Enterprise Architecture Management und Software-Engineering aus einer Hand – wissenschaftlich fundiert und als Partner in Forschungsverbundprojekten. Dabei verbinden wir die organisatorische, technische und psychosoziale Dimension, denn Veränderung gelingt nur, wenn die Menschen mitgehen.

Namhafte Kunden aus Logistik, Finanzen und Industrie begleiten wir als Partner über den gesamten Transformationszyklus, auch über den Go-Live hinaus. Wir hören zu und sprechen die Sprache unserer Kunden. Intern erwarten Dich flache Hierarchien, kurze Entscheidungswege und ein direkter Draht zum Gründer.

Für unser Team KI & Software Engineering suchen wir eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit, die zentrale Datenplattformen in Microsoft Azure bei unseren Kunden konzipiert, aufbaut und fachlich verantwortet – von der Anbindung der Quellsysteme bis zum fertigen Dashboard. Typische Einsatzfelder liegen bei Kunden aus Logistik, Finanzen und Industrie, etwa die Zusammenführung von Unternehmens- und Maschinendaten auf einer gemeinsamen Plattform. Mit wachsender Erfahrung entwickelst Du Dich in der Fachlaufbahn zum Principal Architect Data & Cloud weiter.

Das sind Deine Aufgaben

  • Du konzipierst zentrale Datenplattformen in Microsoft Azure, baust sie auf und entwickelst sie weiter – fachlich verantwortlich gegenüber dem Kunden, eigenständig oder als Senior im Projektteam.

  • Du bindest Unternehmenssysteme und Maschinendaten über Schnittstellen an und modellierst die Daten so, dass sie für KI-Anwendungen, Auswertungen und Dashboards bereitstehen.

  • Du baust für unsere Kunden die Cloud-Infrastruktur mit Infrastructure as Code auf und automatisierst Bereitstellung und Betrieb über CI/CD.

  • Du setzt Sicherheit, Berechtigungen und Mandantentrennung um, sodass jede Nutzergruppe genau die Daten sieht, die sie sehen darf.

  • Du wirkst im Pre-Sales mit, baust Wissen im Team auf und entwickelst unser Daten- und Cloud-Angebot weiter.

Das bringst Du mit

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung als Data Engineer in der Cloud (idealerweise 4+ Jahre), idealerweise in Microsoft Azure, mit sehr guten Kenntnissen in SQL und Python

  • Erfahrung mit Datenintegration über Schnittstellen sowie mit Datenmodellierung und Reporting, idealerweise mit Power BI

  • Erfahrung mit Infrastructure as Code und CI/CD sowie gute Kenntnisse in Cloud-Sicherheit und Berechtigungskonzepten, idealerweise mit Entra ID

  • Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch und Englisch (C1) für die Arbeit mit unseren Kunden

  • Den Wunsch, Dich in der Fachlaufbahn zum Principal Architect Data & Cloud weiterzuentwickeln

Das ist ein Plus

Kein Muss, aber ein Plus – wenn Du die Kriterien oben erfüllst, freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung:

  • Praxis mit Microsoft Fabric – alternativ mit Azure Synapse oder Databricks und die Bereitschaft, auf Fabric umzusteigen

  • Grundlagen in Machine Learning

  • Erfahrung mit Maschinen- und IoT-Daten, z.B. über OPC UA, MQTT oder Azure IoT Hub

  • Branchenkenntnisse in Logistik, Finanzen oder Industrie

Das bieten wir

  • Gehalt und Vorsorge: Zielgehalt von 70.000–100.000 € brutto pro Jahr je nach Erfahrung, inklusive variabler Vergütung nach Projekt- und Unternehmenserfolg, plus betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit Arbeitgeberzuschuss

  • Karriere: Ein klarer Entwicklungspfad zum Principal Architect Data & Cloud mit transparenten Kriterien und regelmäßigen Entwicklungsgesprächen

  • Gestaltungsspielraum: Du prägst Architektur und Vorgehen unserer Datenplattform-Projekte und hast echten Einfluss auf unser Daten- und Cloud-Angebot

  • Weiterbildung und Sichtbarkeit: Persönliches Weiterbildungsbudget, bezahlte Zertifizierungen (z.B. Microsoft Azure und Fabric) und Raum für Konferenzen, Fachbeiträge und Vorträge

  • Reisen: Bis zu 20 % Deiner Arbeitszeit beim Kunden vor Ort

  • Arbeitsort und Flexibilität:
    Büro in Berlin-Wilmersdorf (direkt an der U7/U9 Berliner Straße),
    plus ein Homeoffice-Tag pro Woche,
    flexible Arbeitszeiten mit Arbeitszeitkonto, Voll- oder Teilzeit sowie bis zu 2 Wochen Workation pro Jahr im EU-Ausland

  • Urlaub, Ausstattung und Extras: 28 Tage Urlaub, Mac oder PC nach Wahl, Firmenmobiltelefon, Mobilitätszuschuss, flexible Benefits über ProBonio inklusive Gesundheit und Sport sowie regelmäßige Teamevents

Unsere Werte

Unser Markenkern: Partnerschaft. Ob mit Kunden, Kolleg:innen oder Forschungspartnern – wir arbeiten auf Augenhöhe und auf Dauer. Drei Werte machen das konkret:

Zuhören: Wir verstehen erst, dann gestalten wir. Wir sprechen die Sprache unserer Kunden und nehmen die Menschen mit – im Projekt wie im eigenen Team.

Substanz: Wir arbeiten wissenschaftlich fundiert, sorgfältig und technologisch auf der Höhe der Zeit. Wir empfehlen nur, was wir begründen können.

Verbindlichkeit: Wir übernehmen Verantwortung, als wäre es unser eigenes Unternehmen. Wir halten, was wir zusagen, und bleiben, wenn es darauf ankommt – beim Kunden über den Go-Live hinaus und füreinander im Team.

neoBIM entwickelt KI-Software für die Bau- und Immobilienbranche. Unsere Kunden sind Systembauer, Generalunternehmer und Bauträger.

PLIERA (pliera.com) ist unsere Produktmarke. Unsere Gründer sind Pioniere der Architektursoftware und wissen, wie man ein Produkt zum Branchenstandard macht.

Bisher entstehen fast alle Gespräche über unseren Outbound-Vertrieb und Messen. Das änderst du: Als erste Marketing-Person baust du Inbound auf, bis Systembauer, Generalunternehmer und Bauträger von sich aus eine Demo anfragen. Du arbeitest täglich eng mit Marko zusammen, unserem Principal Architect. Brand Book, Website, Newsletter und klare Regeln für öffentliche Aussagen gibt es schon.

Für wen ist die Rolle ideal?

• Du willst Marketing selbst aufbauen, nicht verwalten

• Du schreibst, drehst und schneidest lieber selbst, als zu briefen

• Du willst sehen, was dein Content im Vertrieb bewirkt

• Du hast Lust auf eine Branche, in der Marketing noch fast niemand richtig macht

Deine Aufgaben

• Positionierung & Story – mit den Gründern festlegen, wie wir über neoBIM und PLIERA sprechen

• Jede Woche LinkedIn-Posts vom Team und von dir

• Klarer Weg zur Demo auf der Website, bei jeder Anfrage ist die Quelle bekannt

• Erste Blogartikel ranken, KI-Suche getestet

Dein Profil

• Aufbau von null – mindestens fünf Jahre B2B-Marketing mit Schwerpunkt Content, mindestens einmal die erste Marketing-Person (Startup oder neue Unit)

• Faktentreue – keine ungeprüften Zahlen, keine Kundenlogos ohne Freigabe

• Deutsch & Englisch – in Wort und Schrift so, dass niemand mehr gegenlesen muss

Nice to have

• Du hast selbst schon gegründet

• Systembauer, Generalunternehmer, Bauträger oder Baustoffhersteller als Kunden, PropTech oder ConTech

• Texte für Gründer geschrieben oder Webinare moderiert

Wichtiger als dein Lebenslauf: Eigeninitiative, Persönlichkeit und Lust aufs Machen.

Arbeitsumfeld und Benefits

jobs.description:
About us

Through our platforms GotPhoto.com and fotograf.de, we help professional photographers simplify and transform the way they work — from photo management and client communication to ordering and payment processing. As the leading e-commerce engine for professional volume photographers and a business backed by EQT, one of the world’s leading private equity firms, we’re powered by a team of 150+ talented and international people building technology that simplifies photographers’ everyday work and helps them focus on capturing meaningful moments.

Join us on our journey to empower photographers like never before.

Do you want to drive turn everyday People administration into a seamless, high-quality experience for every single employee?

  • Talent Spotlight: You help us look after the perfect candidate, from the first review of applications for junior roles to taking notes in interviews, so that the experience stays world-class.

What You’ll Bring

Experience

  • Experience in a Tech Scale-up environment is a bonus.

Skills

Mindset

  • Detail Lover: Accuracy is your quiet superpower.

Why You’ll Love Life at GotPhoto

What Matters to Us

Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds may refrain from applying for positions if they feel they don't meet all qualifications. We strongly encourage you to apply if you’re interested: we're excited to discover how your distinctive experience can enhance our team!

We work as one team. Wherever you come from. However, you identify. We believe in equal opportunities.

jobs.title: Founding Account Executive (Italian Speaker)
jobs.description:
About Sona

Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here (https://www.sona.ai/careers).

About the Role

We're hiring a Founding Account Executive to win Sona's first customers in Italy and open the market for us. This is a senior, seller-first role, and you'll run every conversation with prospects in Italian, from the first call to the close.

Our expansion into Europe is starting now and ramps up through 2027 across key markets. Italy is one of them, and you'll own the go-to-market launch there. Colleagues across Sona will be running the product, operations and other launch activities, so your focus is winning customers, building partnerships and creating the collateral to sell. With no sales team in market yet, you'll work with less support than a typical AE, and the team around you will grow as the market does.


Day to day, you'll decide which Retail and Hospitality accounts to go after, from mid-market through to enterprise, and run consultative sales conversations yourself. You'll also build what a new market needs, including partnerships and Italian-language collateral. The platform is already localised for Italy, and you'll have product and solutions support.

It's early, and the ground will shift as we learn what works. If you want a structured environment with lots of support around you, this won't be the right fit. If you want to shape how Sona sells in Italy from the start, it could be exactly that. The role is office-based in London, with travel to Italy as needed.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the go-to-market launch in Italy and win Sona's first customers, taking each deal from first conversation to close.

  • Build your own pipeline across Retail and Hospitality, from mid-market to enterprise.

  • Run strategic, consultative sales conversations in Italian.

  • Build and run partnerships that open doors in the Italian market.

  • Create the collateral Sona needs to sell in Italy.

  • Work with Sona's Strategy and Expansion Lead on where to focus and how to approach the market.

jobs.title: Growth Ops
jobs.description:
Why this role exists

At Pennylane, Growth Operations is crucial in transforming prospect data and marketing processes into an automated, reliable, and scalable growth engine.

 

We are hiring a Growth Ops to join our Growth team and work at the intersection of business, data, automation, and AI. Your mission: enhance how we identify, enrich, and activate prospects while building tools that boost Marketing and Sales efficiency.

 

You will also contribute to AI adoption by identifying use cases, creating agents and workflows, testing new tools, and empowering teams to use them effectively.

 

🌍 What is Pennylane?

Pennylane is one of France's leading fintech unicorns, creating the financial and accounting operating system for European SMEs and accounting firms.

 

Founded in 2020, we empower business owners to make better decisions and enable accountants to focus on client advisory.

 

A few figures to illustrate our scale and ambition:

 

  • 💻 1.3 million+ SMEs already work with Pennylane.

  • 🤝 7,000+ accounting firms use our platform.

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 1,100+ Pennylaners representing over 25 nationalities.

  • 💰 €400 million+ raised since launch.

  • 🌍 Remote-friendly, international culture as we expand across Europe.

 

What you’ll do

As part of our Growth team, you'll closely collaborate with Marketing, Sales, Product Marketing, Operations, and Product.

 

Build scalable automation workflows

  • Design and maintain complex workflows using n8n

  • Automate prospect scraping, enrichment, scoring, and activation

  • Identify CRM bottlenecks and replace manual processes with scalable solutions

  • Connect our data warehouse with Salesforce to generate opportunities and provide actionable insights to Sales

 

Turn data into growth

  • Improve prospect database quality and usability

  • Build tools to help Marketing and Sales generate and activate qualified leads

  • Support acquisition initiatives: outbound, events, partnerships

  • Monitor project impact on lead generation, conversion, and efficiency

 

Drive AI adoption

  • Identify valuable AI use cases for Growth, Marketing, and Sales

  • Create agents, skills, and reusable workflows

  • Experiment with tools like Dust, Cursor, and Claude Code

  • Support adoption via training, documentation, and pilot programs

 

Connect and optimise our stack

  • Integrate tools such as Salesforce, Modjo, Dust, and Livestorm

  • Translate business needs into technical solutions

  • Own projects from scoping to deployment and iteration

  • Ensure compliance with GDPR, CNIL, security, and data governance

 

What you bring

  • Hands-on experience in Growth Ops, Marketing Ops, Revenue Ops, or automation, ideally in B2B SaaS or a scale-up

  • Strong proficiency with n8n and complex, multi-tool workflows

  • Ability to translate business challenges into tech solutions

  • Familiarity with CRM systems, prospect data, scraping, enrichment, and scoring

  • Proven record of impactful automation projects

  • Practical experience using AI tools and supporting adoption

  • Strong communication and project management skills

  • Autonomy, curiosity, and an ownership mindset

  • Professional working proficiency in English

  • Bonus: Experience with SEO, SEA, or the broader acquisition funnel

 

🛠️ Tools and environment

You’ll use tools like n8n, Salesforce, Modjo, Dust, and Livestorm and experiment with solutions such as Cursor, Claude Code, and MCPs.

 

What you can expect

  • A role combining Growth, automation, data, and AI

  • End-to-end ownership with measurable business impact

  • Opportunity to build systems from scratch

  • Key role in shaping automation and AI practices

  • Close collaboration with cross-functional teams

  • A demanding, supportive, execution- and learning-focused environment

 

📍 Location and working model

Permanent position based in Paris on a hybrid basis

 

🔎 Our recruitment process

  • Talent Acquisition interview (30 min, remote)

  • Hiring Manager interview (1 hour, remote)

  • Case study & debrief (1 hour, remote)

  • Final interview with a Marketing leader (45 min, remote)

  • Team-fit interview (1 hour, in person)

 

🌈 Our commitment to diversity and inclusion

Pennylane is committed to an inclusive, supportive work environment with equal opportunities for all candidates, regardless of background, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other personal characteristic.

 

If this role excites you and you believe you could add value, we encourage you to apply—even if you do not meet every requirement.
